clue.text: Award for second fiddle announced after brass

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out loud, so we want a word that sounds like the fiddle word
after places the spoken piece behind the metal piece in the answer

blocks.note: brass and silver are both slang for money or coins
to fiddle with something is to meddle with it

explanation.surface: A violinist who plays second fiddle gets a prize announced once the brass section has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second fiddle' and 'brass' suggest an orchestra, but the definition is 'Award for second', and brass is money.
explanation.definitionFit: The runner-up in an Olympic event receives the metal prize below gold.

clue.text: Raised in Africa, a significant biblical figure

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters read upwards, so from bottom to top
in says the letters sit inside the run of clue words that follows

blocks.note: the letters straddling the end of Africa, the lone a and the start of significant

explanation.surface: Someone important to the Bible was brought up in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac is the son of Abraham in Genesis, a major patriarch of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Futile incarcerating bad, bad guy

indicators.note: incarcerating means locking up, so one word holds the other inside it

blocks.note: a futile effort is a vain one
bad as in ill, sick or harmful

explanation.surface: It is pointless to lock up a bad man.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'bad' is the trick: the first is the wordplay, the second starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain is the wicked character in a story or a criminal, the classic bad guy.

clue.text: Country, one moving fast, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: by the sound of it says to go by how the phrase is pronounced rather than spelt

blocks.note: someone who rushes about is a rusher

explanation.surface: A country seems to be named after somebody in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia is the largest nation on Earth, spanning Eastern Europe and northern Asia.

clue.text: Great thinker, intense I suspect

indicators.note: suspect read as an adjective means dodgy or unreliable, so the letters are not in a trustworthy order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a brilliant mind is a very intense person.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein, the physicist behind relativity, is the byword for genius.

clue.text: Desert with a river in middle of Qatar

indicators.note: middle of keeps only the central letters of the country name, dropping its ends
in places the first pieces inside the letters taken from the country

blocks.note: the three central letters of Qatar
taken as written
the Cam is the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A desert with a river running through the heart of Qatar.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cam is the river at Cambridge, a crossword favourite; the clue's 'a' and the river go inside the Qatar letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atacama in northern Chile is among the driest places in the world.

clue.text: Beneath tower, search frantically for jumper

indicators.note: in a down clue, beneath places the second piece below the first in the column
done frantically means done in a wild disordered way, so the letters get thrown about

blocks.note: a steeple is a church tower
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hunts desperately under a church tower for a lost sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like a sweater (the British word for a pullover), but here it is a horse that jumps fences.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeplechaser is a horse or runner competing in a race over fences and ditches, so a jumper.

clue.text: Priceless work Somalian lost

indicators.note: something lost is astray and out of place, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A valuable painting has been mislaid by someone from Somalia.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo's portrait in the Louvre is so valuable it is effectively beyond any price.

clue.text: Rebel, Republican in transition

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
something undergoing gradual change is evolutionary

explanation.surface: A rebel is a Republican who is changing sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolutionary is someone who rises up against the established order or government.

clue.text: Follow the track when he has departed

indicators.note: once he has departed, the letters of the word he are taken out of the phrase

blocks.note: a rail is a track, read with the article attached
taken as written

explanation.surface: Track someone along a path once he has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follow the track' reads as one instruction, but only 'Follow' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail someone is to tail or pursue them, a verb meaning to follow.

clue.text: A hole added to belt out in Asian country

indicators.note: added to means the first piece is attached on to the end of the second

blocks.note: to belt out a song is to sing it loudly
a pore is a tiny hole in the skin

explanation.surface: Someone punches an extra hole in a belt while abroad in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belt' looks like a strap with holes, but 'belt out' means sing loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: Singapore is a city-state at the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: It sure rattles carrying tea service!

indicators.note: rattling something shakes it up, so these letters are jumbled
carrying means holding, so the shuffled letters hold the drink inside them

blocks.note: taken as written
cha is an informal British word for tea

explanation.surface: A tea service clatters as it is carried around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea service' reads as a set of cups, but the definition is just 'service', a church one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eucharist is the Christian sacrament of Holy Communion, celebrated as a church rite.

clue.text: Reading odd parts, all warm to mission

indicators.note: reading only the odd parts means taking the first, third, fifth letters and so on

blocks.note: letters one, three, five and seven of all warm
the ninth letter of the run, the last of to

explanation.surface: Someone reads odd bits aloud, all warmly welcomed to a mission.
explanation.walkthrough: Odd letters of 'all warm to' run across all three words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo in San Antonio, Texas, was a Spanish Catholic mission before its famous siege.

clue.text: Hidden pavilion in Los Angeles?

indicators.note: a pavilion in a city is read as the city name placed before the shelter word

blocks.note: LA is the standard abbreviation for the Californian city
a pavilion can be a large ornamental tent

explanation.surface: Is there a secret marquee tucked away somewhere in Los Angeles?
explanation.definitionFit: Latent means present but not yet visible or active, as in concealed.

clue.text: Various patterns in area crossing nave

indicators.note: various suggests assorted different forms, so the letters take on a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A church has many different designs in the part that cuts across its main hall.
explanation.definitionFit: In a cross-shaped church, the transept is the arm lying across the main body at right angles.

clue.text: Sweet rum and Asti I mixed up

indicators.note: mixing things up stirs them together, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook makes a dessert by stirring together rum and sparkling wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Asti is an Italian sparkling wine, which suits the Italian dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian dessert, and sweet is the British word for a pudding course.

clue.text: Brilliant solving

blocks.note: first meaning: excellent, a British informal term of praise
second meaning: working out a code or puzzle

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like praise for a solver, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for excellent and also the act of breaking a code or puzzle.

clue.text: Those in temporary shelter imbibing hot drink

indicators.note: imbibing means taking in, so the first word swallows the second

blocks.note: people sleeping in tents are campers
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: People under canvas are knocking back something warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot drink' looks like the definition, but 'hot' is the H.
explanation.definitionFit: Champers is British informal slang for champagne, a bubbly alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Seed with long head

blocks.note: to pine for something is to long for it
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A seed with an elongated top.
explanation.definitionFit: Pine nuts are the edible kernels of certain pine trees, used in pesto.

clue.text: Some animal assessed after a turn — it has been cured!

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the words that follow is wanted
after a turn the letters face the other way and read backwards

blocks.note: the end of animal and start of assessed

explanation.surface: An animal is examined after falling ill, and it has recovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cured' in the surface means healed; in the definition it means preserved with salt.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a sausage preserved by salting and air-drying, so it has been cured meat.

clue.text: Name a place south of capital in Paraguay

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of puts the place word below the capital letter
the capital of a word is its first, upper-case letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of Paraguay
a point is a particular place or spot

explanation.surface: Choose a town lying south of the capital city of Paraguay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests Asunción, but it means a capital letter. A sits first, then P, then POINT below.
explanation.definitionFit: To name someone to a post is to appoint or nominate them.

clue.text: Shooter clocked in outskirts of Riga

indicators.note: the outskirts are the edges, so only the outer letters of the city name are kept

blocks.note: clocking in at work means arriving there
the first and last letters of Riga

explanation.surface: A gunman was spotted on the edge of the Latvian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooter' suggests a gun; it is something that shoots photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers shoot pictures, so the device that takes them is a shooter.

clue.text: A motive lacking in each crime

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the abbreviated word is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
a motive is a reason for doing something
EA is the standard abbreviation for each

explanation.surface: Detectives cannot find a motive in any of the offences.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the criminal offence of deliberately setting fire to property.

clue.text: Restriction in first of colours, light blue

indicators.note: first of keeps only the opening letter of the following word

blocks.note: the opening letter of colours
a lamp is a light
feeling blue is feeling down, low in spirits

explanation.surface: A limit on the shades available, starting with pale blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light blue' looks like one colour, but the two words split into separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A clampdown is a severe crackdown or official curbing of some activity.

clue.text: Small tree, old as it happens

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a live broadcast goes out as events happen

explanation.surface: A little tree that, as it turns out, is ancient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As it happens' reads as 'incidentally', but means broadcast in real time.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive is a short evergreen Mediterranean tree grown for its fruit and oil.

clue.text: Dear old flame, broody

blocks.note: an old flame is a former partner, an ex
brooding is thinking deeply and gloomily

explanation.surface: A letter beginning 'Dear' to a former lover who is moody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' looks like a greeting or term of endearment, but it means costly.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage dear means costly or high-priced, as in a dear shop.

clue.text: Colder in Canada in every respect, originally

indicators.note: originally points to the origin of each word, its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letters of in, Canada, in, every and respect

explanation.surface: Canada is chillier in every way, at least at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Icier means more frozen or chilly, a comparative adjective of temperature.

clue.text: Moving target I pass in events for young men

indicators.note: a moving thing changes position, so the letters shift into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shooter walks past a moving target at some sporting events.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag party is the British name for a bachelor party held before a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Stag parties are pre-wedding celebrations for a groom and his male friends.
